title: Scalar mates and counits in a finite ordered tower
statement:
Let $d\geq0$. For $0\leq r\leq d$ and $R\in\{A,B\}$ let $\mathcal C_{r,R}$ be categories, and let $T_r:\mathcal C_{r,A}\to\mathcal C_{r,B}$ be functors. For $r<d$ fix adjunctions $L_{r,R}:\mathcal C_{r+1,R}\rightleftarrows\mathcal C_{r,R}:W_{r,R}$, with $L_{r,R}$ left adjoint and actual counit $e_{r,R}$. Suppose given natural isomorphisms $b_r:T_rL_{r,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{r,B}T_{r+1}$ and $a_r:T_{r+1}W_{r,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}W_{r,B}T_r$ such that $a_r$ is the mate of $b_r^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Starting from the identity adjunction, form the actual ordered composite adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]
$$\mathcal F_{0,R}=\mathcal G_{0,R}=1_{\mathcal C_{0,R}},\quad \mathcal F_{r+1,R}=\mathcal F_{r,R}L_{r,R},\quad \mathcal G_{r+1,R}=W_{r,R}\mathcal G_{r,R}.$$
Write their counits as $\mathcal E_{0,R}=1$ and
$$\mathcal E_{r+1,R}=\mathcal E_{r,R}\circ\mathcal F_{r,R}(e_{r,R}\mathcal G_{r,R}).$$
Define $B_0=A_0=1$ and
$$B_{r+1}=\mathcal F_{r,B}(b_r)\circ B_rL_{r,A},\qquad A_{r+1}=W_{r,B}(A_r)\circ a_r\mathcal G_{r,A}.$$
Then $A_d:T_d\mathcal G_{d,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G_{d,B}T_0$ is the mate of $B_d^{-1}$ for those composite adjunctions, and for every $K\in\mathcal C_{0,A}$,
$$\mathcal E_{d,B,T_0K}\circ\mathcal F_{d,B}(A_d(K))\circ B_d(\mathcal G_{d,A}K)=T_0(\mathcal E_{d,A,K}).$$
At $d=0$ all functors, comparisons and counits are identities. No identification of a composite left functor with a compactification, or of a composite right functor with a twisted pullback, is part of this assertion.

proof.text: For every $r\leq d$, compose the adjunction $L_{r,R}\dashv W_{r,R}$ (when $r<d$) with the already constructed $\mathcal F_{r,R}\dashv\mathcal G_{r,R}$, in that order. The composite-adjunction formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] gives $\mathcal F_{r,R}L_{r,R}\dashv W_{r,R}\mathcal G_{r,R}$ with actual counit $\mathcal E_{r,R}\circ\mathcal F_{r,R}(e_{r,R}\mathcal G_{r,R})$. Its identity-adjunction clause starts the recursion at $r=0$. Thus these are exactly the ordered adjunctions and counits in the statement. We prove by induction on $r$ that $B_r,A_r$ are natural isomorphisms and that $A_r$ is the mate of $B_r^{-1}$ for these adjunctions.

source.place: Charts, iterated projective-line integration; ordered counits made explicit using Stacks 0DV0 (lemma-compose-counits)

proof.text: At $r=0$ the left and right composite functors are identities, their units and counits are identities, and $B_0=A_0=1_{T_0}$. In the component formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], take both adjunctions to be the identity adjunctions of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and take $G=H=T_0$. All three arrows defining the mate of $B_0^{-1}=1_{T_0}$ are identities; its mate is therefore $A_0$. This also proves the asserted zero-length case, without requiring $T_0$ itself to be the identity functor.

source.place: Charts, iterated projective-line integration; identity base case for the finite iteration

proof.text:
Suppose the inductive claim holds at $r<d$. Whiskering an isomorphism preserves its inverse: applying a functor to its two inverse equations gives the inverse equations for its image, and right whiskering evaluates the same equations at the relevant objects. Hence the two recursion formulas define natural isomorphisms $B_{r+1},A_{r+1}$. Reversing the two factors of $B_{r+1}$ gives
$$B_{r+1}^{-1}=(B_r^{-1}L_{r,A})\circ\mathcal F_{r,B}(b_r^{-1}).$$
Indeed, composing this expression with $\mathcal F_{r,B}(b_r)\circ(B_rL_{r,A})$ in either order cancels the adjacent inverse pairs.

source.place: Charts, iterated projective-line integration; elementary inverse calculation for the successor comparison

proof.text:
Apply clause (2), pasting along the adjunctions, of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Make the substitutions
$$(L_1,R_1)=(L_{r,A},W_{r,A}),\quad(L_3,R_3)=(\mathcal F_{r,A},\mathcal G_{r,A}),$$
$$(L_2,R_2)=(L_{r,B},W_{r,B}),\quad(L_4,R_4)=(\mathcal F_{r,B},\mathcal G_{r,B}),$$
$$G=T_{r+1},\quad H=T_r,\quad K=T_0,\quad\alpha=b_r^{-1},\quad\beta=B_r^{-1}.$$
Here $\alpha:L_{r,B}T_{r+1}\to T_rL_{r,A}$ has mate $a_r$ by hypothesis, while $\beta:\mathcal F_{r,B}T_r\to T_0\mathcal F_{r,A}$ has mate $A_r$ by induction. The pasted left square $(\beta L_1)\circ(L_4\alpha)$ is exactly the inverse computed in step 3. Its mate is
$$(R_2\beta^\flat)\circ(\alpha^\flat R_3)=W_{r,B}(A_r)\circ a_r\mathcal G_{r,A}=A_{r+1}.$$
The adjunctions used by that clause are the same ordered composites as in step 1, with their actual counits, so no change-of-adjunction identification is needed. This closes the induction.

source.place: Charts, iterated projective-line integration; binary mate pasting iterated in the stated order

proof.text:
Use [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit] with $L_1=\mathcal F_{d,A}$, $R_1=\mathcal G_{d,A}$, $L_2=\mathcal F_{d,B}$, $R_2=\mathcal G_{d,B}$, $G=T_d$, $H=T_0$, $\alpha=B_d^{-1}$, and its mate $\beta=A_d$. For $K\in\mathcal C_{0,A}$ it gives
$$\mathcal E_{d,B,T_0K}\circ\mathcal F_{d,B}(A_d(K))=T_0(\mathcal E_{d,A,K})\circ B_d^{-1}(\mathcal G_{d,A}K).$$
Precompose both sides with $B_d(\mathcal G_{d,A}K)$. The adjacent factors $B_d^{-1}(\mathcal G_{d,A}K)\circ B_d(\mathcal G_{d,A}K)$ cancel to the identity, giving exactly the required formula. The argument used only the ordered composite adjunctions, and makes none of the geometric identifications excluded by the statement.
